chapters.title: A ruler short
panels: The Proving Ground is making benches for its new reading corner.
A carpenter's brass ruler vanishes between the morning chai and the first cut.
No wood is missing, but every bench mark is one finger too short.
Mira notices the marks were drawn with a blue pencil, not the carpenter's red one.
A blue pencil lies beside the school's model bridge, sharpened to a point.
Dev measures the bridge and finds its span matches the shortened bench exactly.
On Sunday, they find the ruler inside the bridge model. A note on it says: measure the space between people.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals two pencil dots on the ruler, set a bench's length apart.

chapters.title: Room for two
panels: Mira tests the dotted length against the reading corner. It leaves room for a second chair.
The carpenter says no second chair was ordered.
A student brings a sketch showing pairs of readers sharing each bench.
The sketch has no signature, but its paper came from the Ground's notice board.
Dev finds a blank pinhole where one notice used to hang.
The missing notice invited visitors to tell a story with a stranger.
On Sunday, the author steps forward: the quiet librarian. She asks why the invitation vanished before anyone could answer.
chapters.bonus: The bonus panel reveals a reply tucked under the notice board: 'I will come.'

chapters.title: The hidden reply
panels: The reply is written on wrapping paper from the canteen.
The canteen keeper remembers lending a pen to a visitor with a rolled map.
The map shows the Ground before its reading corner existed.
One room on the map is labelled for listening, then crossed out.
Mira looks through old plans and finds the room was never built.
The visitor had come to ask whether the idea still had a place here.
On Sunday, the visitor returns. She once drew the plan, but the map she carries is missing its final sheet.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals the sheet's outline pressed into the back of the map.

chapters.title: A place to listen
panels: The final sheet turns up beneath a stack of fabric samples.
It shows no room at all: just two benches facing a courtyard tree.
The librarian laughs. The reading corner already has the perfect tree.
Mira sets the brass ruler beside the drawing and sees both pencil dots line up.
The shortened marks had been a clumsy rehearsal for a kinder layout.
The carpenter admits he moved the ruler to the bridge model to keep it safe.
On Sunday, the benches are ready. One is still bare, with a card that reads: reserved for a story nobody has told yet.
chapters.bonus: The bonus panel shows the first two readers taking that seat together.

chapters.title: The first story
panels: A visitor sits beside the librarian and describes the Ground's first rainy opening day.
Her account differs from the old plaque by a single date.
Dev checks a photograph: the umbrellas prove the visitor right.
The plaque was copied from a draft, not the opening record.
Mira finds the signed record folded inside a book of carpentry patterns.
The carpenter offers to make a small new plaque, with room for another correction someday.
On Sunday, the reading corner opens with two benches and one honest date. Under the new plaque is a small mark none of them made.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals the mark is a tiny measuring scale for future makers.
